summary: Task 4 is a JSON-only locale edit verified by the existing parity gate (frontend/scripts/check-locales.mjs via pnpm prebuild). The parity gate is the correct primary test for the key-set acceptance criteria and the gate is adequate for that purpose: collectKeySet flattens nested objects to dotted paths and compareKeySets returns symmetric missingInA/missingInB diffs, exiting 1 on any asymmetry with a stderr line that names the missing keys. I re-verified both Smoke branches end-to-end on the post-commit tree: (a) `pnpm prebuild` exits 0 in the current state; (b) deleting `errors.bot.connect.429` from en.json and re-running produces exit 1 with the exact message `Keys present in uk.json but missing in en.json: errors.bot.connect.429`; restoring the key returns exit 0. The post-edit success path is therefore confirmed and the failure path is confirmed to detect the precise deletion path called out in the task spec. Three gaps remain: (1) the Smoke sanity-check result has not yet been recorded in `decisions.md` (there is no Task 4 section in decisions.md at all yet — the prompt notes this is intentional and will be written after this review, so this is flagged as informational rather than as a finding against the implementer); (2) the parity gate enforces only KEY parity, not VALUE content, so three acceptance criteria are not mechanically gated by `pnpm prebuild` alone (`bot.disconnect.modal.body` containing the `{username}` placeholder; `errors.bot.connect.409` not leaking foreign project identity; AC22 exact-leaves contract — both locales could symmetrically add a forbidden key like `errors.bot.connect.401` and the parity gate would still pass); (3) the TDD anchor as currently written tests structural symmetry only, not behavioral consumption of the keys (e.g., a Vue-i18n runtime check that `t('bot.disconnect.modal.body', { username: 'foo' })` produces a string containing `@foo`). For a JSON-only data task in Wave 1 whose downstream consumers (Tasks 5, 9) will exercise the runtime behavior themselves, the test-first parity flow is acceptable in spirit; the missing value-level checks are recommended as cheap jq/grep assertions that the implementer should record alongside the Smoke output in decisions.md.

findings.finding: The parity gate (check-locales.mjs) enforces only flat-key-set symmetry, not value content. Three acceptance criteria are therefore NOT covered by `pnpm prebuild` alone and are not currently verified by any recorded check: (a) AC `bot.disconnect.modal.body uses the {username} named interpolation placeholder` — both locales could drop `{username}` symmetrically and parity would still pass; (b) AC `errors.bot.connect.409 carries no foreign project name, owner email, or other identifier in either locale (AC6, R2)` — parity gate cannot inspect string content; (c) AC22 exact-leaves contract (`errors.bot.connect` = {400,422,500,502,409,429,generic}, `testMessage` = {422,502,generic}, `disconnect` = {404,generic}, NO 401 anywhere) — if both locales symmetrically added a forbidden key (e.g. `errors.bot.connect.401`), parity gate exits 0 and the AC22 contract silently breaks. I confirmed the keys are correct in the current commit by direct inspection, but no automated assertion will catch a future regression on these three ACs from the existing gate alone.
findings.recommendation:
Record three lightweight content checks in decisions.md `Verification` for Task 4 alongside the Smoke pnpm prebuild result. All three are one-liners and pass on the current commit:
  jq -e '.bot.disconnect.modal.body | test("\\{username\\}")' frontend/i18n/locales/en.json frontend/i18n/locales/uk.json  # AC19 placeholder presence in both locales
  jq -r '.errors.bot.connect."409"' frontend/i18n/locales/en.json frontend/i18n/locales/uk.json  # then visual review: confirm string carries no @-handle, no project name, no email
  jq -e '(.errors.bot.connect | keys | sort) == ["400","409","422","429","500","502","generic"] and (.errors.bot.testMessage | keys | sort) == ["422","502","generic"] and (.errors.bot.disconnect | keys | sort) == ["404","generic"]' frontend/i18n/locales/en.json frontend/i18n/locales/uk.json  # AC22 exact-leaves contract, both locales
Running these against the current commit returns true/0 for the first and third and the expected generic-409 strings for the second — they document the AC22 / AC19 / AC6+R2 coverage that parity alone misses without adding a new test file. Optional follow-up (defer to Task 9 owners): consider promoting the AC22 exact-leaves check into check-locales.mjs as a constant inventory assertion for the `bot.*` namespace so future regressions fail at prebuild rather than at QA.

findings.finding: Per test-master TDD-anchor quality criteria, an anchor that verifies only key-set / string-presence is a structural assertion, not a behavioral one. The current anchor (parity gate exit code) verifies 'the flat key sets match' — it does not verify 'Vue-i18n actually resolves these paths at runtime', 'the {username} interpolation actually produces a string containing the passed handle', or 'useApiError() resolves errors.bot.connect.422 → "Token is invalid or revoked"'. For a JSON-only Wave-1 data task whose runtime consumers (Tasks 5 and 9) will exercise the strings in their own Vue component tests, this is acceptable in spirit and the test-first flow (prebuild → break one locale → expect exit 1 with named key → restore → expect exit 0) IS faithfully described by the task spec and demonstrably works (I re-ran the failing-state branch and confirmed exit 1 with the precise `Keys present in uk.json but missing in en.json: errors.bot.connect.429` message, then restored to exit 0). Calling out as minor for visibility, not as a blocker.
findings.recommendation: No code change required for this task. When Task 9 (Bot page) is implemented, ensure at least one component-level test exercises `t('bot.disconnect.modal.body', { username: 'demo' })` end-to-end and asserts the rendered string contains `@demo` — that closes the behavioral loop the JSON-only parity gate cannot cover. Optionally, add a single line to decisions.md for Task 4 noting that runtime behavior (interpolation, useApiError chain) is deferred to Task 5 / Task 9 component tests, so the deferral is explicit rather than implicit.
